#1.1.Create a function for summary statistics

Create a function
```{r}
summary_statistics <- function(x) {

  result <- list(
    Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Standard_Deviation = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Variance = var(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Minimum = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Maximum = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Range = range(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  return(result)
}
```


#1.2.Apply the function to a variable
We will use the iris dataset.

```{r}
data("iris")
View(iris)

data(iris)

summary_statistics(iris$Sepal.Length)

summary_statistics(iris$Petal.Length)

```
Expected interpretation
- The mean tells us the average sepal length.
- The median identifies the middle sepal length.
- The standard deviation tells us how dispersed the values are.
- The variance measures variability in squared units.
- The minimum and maximum identify the smallest and largest observations.
- The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of observations.
Conclusion: The function can be reused for different numerical variables without writing all the statistical calculations repeatedly.

2.Create a function for a two-sample t-test

2.1.What is a two-sample t-test?
A two-sample t-test compares the means of two independent groups to determine whether there is a statistically significant difference between them.

2.2.Create a Function

```{r}
two_sample_test <- function(x, y) {

  result <- t.test(
    x,
    y,
    alternative = "two.sided",
    var.equal = FALSE
  )

  return(result)
}
```
2.3. Apply the function to iris dataset

```{r}
data(iris)

# Extract the first group
group1 <- iris$Sepal.Length[
  iris$Species == "setosa"
]

# Extract the second group
group2 <- iris$Sepal.Length[
  iris$Species == "versicolor"
]

# Apply our function
two_sample_test(group1, group2)
```
2.3. Extract individual results

```{r}
test_result <- two_sample_test(group1, group2)

# Display t-statistic
test_result$statistic

# Display p-value
test_result$p.value

# Display confidence interval
test_result$conf.int

# Display group means
mean(group1)
mean(group2)
```
Conclusion:

Two-Sample t-test was conducted to determine whether there is a significant difference in mean sepal length between Setosa and Versicolor species in the Iris dataset. The results showed a statistically significant difference between the two groups (t = -10.521, df = 86.538, p < 0.001). The mean sepal length for Setosa was 5.006 cm, while that of Versicolor was 5.936 cm. The estimated mean difference was -0.930 cm, with a 95% confidence interval ranging from -1.106 to -0.754 cm. Therefore, the null hypothesis was rejected, indicating that Versicolor flowers have significantly longer sepals on average than Setosa flowers.
